passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of the novel antihypertensive agent, Hypotensol, in adults with stage 1 hypertension. Eighty participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive either Hypotensol (n=40) or a matched placebo (n=40) for 12 weeks. Baseline measurements of systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were taken using an automated cuff after a 5‑minute rest period. Following the 12‑week intervention, participants returned for a final assessment. Table 1 summarizes the mean SBP and DBP values for each group at baseline and after treatment. The Hypotensol group demonstrated a mean SBP reduction of 12 mmHg and a DBP decrease of 6 mmHg, whereas the placebo group showed negligible changes. The authors concluded that Hypotensol lowered both SBP and DBP more than placebo in this trial; no statistical test is reported.
stem: Which of the following best describes the data presented in Table 1?

options.A: The placebo group had higher baseline SBP than the Hypotensol group.
options.B: The placebo group had a greater reduction in DBP than Hypotensol.
options.C: Both groups experienced similar reductions in SBP.
options.D: The Hypotensol group showed a greater reduction in SBP than the placebo group.

explanation: Correct: D) SBP fell 12 mmHg with Hypotensol (150 to 138) versus 1 mmHg with placebo (149 to 148). Why the others are wrong: A) Baseline SBP was 149 for placebo, slightly lower than 150 for Hypotensol. B) DBP fell 6 mmHg with Hypotensol (95 to 89) and 1 mmHg with placebo. C) The SBP reductions were 12 and 1 mmHg, not similar.
trap: Treating a 1 mmHg baseline difference as meaningful and reading it in the wrong direction; the baselines (150 vs 149) are nearly equal and the Hypotensol group's was higher.

stem: What is the between-group difference in mean SBP reduction (Hypotensol minus placebo)?
explanation: Correct: B) Hypotensol reduced SBP by 12 mmHg and placebo by 1 mmHg, so the difference in reduction is 12 - 1 = 11 mmHg. Why the others are wrong: A) 1 mmHg is the placebo reduction alone. C) 12 mmHg ignores the placebo change. D) 13 mmHg adds the two reductions instead of subtracting.
trap: Reporting the raw 12 mmHg drop in the drug group and ignoring the 1 mmHg placebo change; the group difference subtracts them.
